findings.scope: Objective-level reassessment. The accepted reduction covers exactly the class C_2 (finite bipartite, at least one edge, no 4-cycle, some bipartition with one side of maximum degree at most two) and Problem 1.5 for all finite simple base graphs with an edge. Obligations 000001 (root decision), 000003 (girth-six graphs outside C_2) and 000004 (case-split bridge) are untouched. The retire disposition applies only to strategy reduce-and-translate on node-000001 within this bounded attempt; it closes nothing. This approval does not cover: the mathematical content of the sign-model hypothesis; the description in what_changed of the admission review of proposal-000002 (that review is not delivered and cannot be verified here; the reassessment's disposition does not depend on it); Section 5 item 2 of the proof file (transfer of known cases, relying on undelivered Zhao 2026); or any claim that the root statement or Problem 1.5 is open.
findings.statement: The subject is a scientific reassessment of objective-000001 after move 1 of node-000001, bound to the root claim 43d81023... (every finite bipartite H with an edge and no 4-cycle satisfies t(H,W) >= t(K_2,W)^{e(H)} for every graphon W). Nothing new is established about the root statement: no decision in either direction is delivered, and the reassessment does not claim one. The only accepted evidence is acceptance-000001 for checkpoint-000001 (kind reduction, milestone c2-reduces-to-problem-1-5, claims_openness false, outcome reduction): the premise on C_2 (obligation-000002) holds iff the 1-subdivision of every finite simple graph with an edge is Sidorenko (CKLL Problem 1.5, stated verbatim in the delivered full text a662797f...). I rechecked that proof independently rather than by authority: the Hom-sum identity |Hom(H,G)| = sum_{phi in Hom(H-v,G)} deg(phi(u)); CKLL Lemma 3.4 (its averaging step d(G_{i+1}) >= d(G_i) + d/(2(|V(G_i)|-1)) and the harmonic-sum contradiction at t=(1-2^{-6})n are correct) giving G_0 with n_0 >= 2^{-6}n, min degree >= d/4 and p(G_0) >= d/(4n_0) >= p/4; the chain |Hom(H,G)| >= (d/4)|Hom(H-v,G_0)| >= (pn/4)(2^{-6}n)^{h-1}(p/4)^{m-1} = 4^{-m}2^{-6(h-1)}n^h p^m; the vertex-splitting bounded-degree reduction (injectivity of pi∘h, |V(G')| <= 2|V(G)|, |E(G')|=|E(G)|, factor 2^{h-2m}) followed by the tensor power trick over all hosts; Proposition B (i)=>(ii) (subdivision vertices form a side of degree two; a 4-cycle x a x' b would be a double edge of F) and (ii)=>(i) (peel X-vertices of degree <= 1, whose degrees are stable since X is independent, then isolated Y-vertices; rebuild by Lemma A (<=) and the isolated-vertex remark; the residual is empty, giving a forest of stars, or isomorphic to S(F) with F simple exactly because H has no 4-cycle). No gap found. The reassessment then correctly records: (a) the strategy reduce-and-translate on node-000001 is retired because its single, nonclosing milestone is met by acceptance-000001 and the node's statement is now the image problem, which CKLL describe as outside the reach of current methods; (b) remaining_obligation_ids = all four, consistent with checkpoint-000001 and the context; (c) a next hypothesis on obligation-000003 (the pairwise sign model of the reported construction is identically 1 on girth-six patterns, conditional on the rank-layer limit analogue) is recorded as a hypothesis with a failure signal and success criterion, not as a result.
